title: Amundsen reaches the South Pole, 1911
summary: From the hut at Framheim on the Bay of Whales, Amundsen laid depots at 80, 81 and 82 degrees south in February and March 1911, and set out for the Pole on 19 October with five men, four sledges and 52 dogs. They climbed the Axel Heiberg Glacier in November and reached the Pole on 14 December 1911, and were back at Framheim on 25 January 1912, 99 days out.

events.label: Framheim, on the Bay of Whales
events.text: The hut was finished in late January 1911 on the Great Ice Barrier (the Ross Ice Shelf). The place is drawn to the bay, not surveyed from a source.

events.label: The South Pole: the Norwegian flag
events.text: Amundsen, Bjaaland, Hanssen, Hassel and Wisting reached the Pole at about 3 pm and camped at Polheim near it.
